comparator.name: Global Sustainability Science
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–27 regulations govern the September 2026 entry. The 135 EC major comprises a 60 EC common core and 75 EC of track requirements and major choices. The illustrative Water, Climate & Ecosystems route follows official track order. The Philosophy of Science and Ethics course, ordinary Consultancy Project, Landscape Ecology and Nature Conservation, and Environmental Chemistry and Health illustrate the permitted non-track choices. The remaining 45 EC is the optional course profile, including at least 15 EC at level 2 or 3. This curriculum example records the credit structure and academic progression. Individual course timeslots are confirmed at registration.

components.note: Pass Research Skills GSS and the Regional Integration Project and participate fully in Statistics GSS before starting.

components.note: This advanced track course requires 90 EC and assumes prior study of environmental chemistry, global climate change and ecological field research.

components.name: Bachelor's thesis Water, Climate & Ecosystems
components.note: Before the 15 EC individual thesis, pass the specified common courses, the introductory and intermediate track requirements and at least one advanced major elective. Active participation is required in Statistics GSS, consultancy and the advanced track course.

components.name: Consultancy Project
components.note: The project works on an external organisation’s sustainability question. Entry requires at least 90 EC, including Sustainability Challenges and the two integration projects.

components.name: Optional course profile
components.note: Choose 45 EC, with at least 15 EC at intermediate or advanced level. Options include extra major courses, a minor, study abroad or an internship. External courses require approval.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Two additional generator-backed directions are coherent and feasible after the closest match: Governance & Societal Transformation and a combined Business & Innovation plus Energy & Resources route. Both are substantively distinct and exceed the 30-EC pairwise course-difference floor, so the maximum of three UCR alternatives is reached.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both use interdisciplinary concepts to examine sustainability challenges. UCR introduces planetary boundaries and scientific tools through modelling and laboratory work.
Both study interactions among natural processes. UCR focuses on Earth systems, geology and field evidence.
Both examine climate processes, impacts and possible responses. Utrecht deepens the topic within the track.
Both examine biodiversity and ecological processes. Utrecht specialises in landscape ecology and conservation at advanced level.
Both examine water in soils and related natural systems. UCR focuses on soils and shallow aquifers, while Utrecht integrates water and ecosystem processes.
Utrecht surveys social-science approaches to sustainability. UCR develops related perspectives across economics, governance and environmental justice courses.
Both examine sustainability transitions, actors and possible interventions. Utrecht brings the perspectives together in a project. UCR focuses on governance and policy evaluation.
Both use chemistry to investigate environmental problems. UCR focuses on recovering materials and assessing remediation processes.
Both examine chemical processes and contaminants in environmental systems. Utrecht gives additional attention to human exposure and health.
Both develop mathematical tools for analysing systems. Utrecht embeds the tools in its sustainability programme.
Both develop research design and evidence skills. UCR adds statistical inference and quantitative analysis within this course.
Both develop statistical inference and hypothesis testing. UCR gives greater emphasis to mathematical foundations and simulation.
Both integrate evidence and disciplinary perspectives in an applied sustainability project. Utrecht uses fieldwork and stakeholder research on Texel. UCR investigates sustainability campaigns.
Utrecht requires a dedicated ecological field research course. UCR develops related field and laboratory skills in courses including Soils & Aquifers.
Utrecht offers philosophy of science and ethics as an intermediate major choice.
Utrecht requires a 15 EC individual thesis. UCR’s 15 EC optional independent research is shown separately from the scheduled courses.
Utrecht requires a separate consultancy project addressing an external organisation’s question.
Choose 45 EC, with at least 15 EC at intermediate or advanced level. Options include extra major courses, a minor, study abroad or an internship. External courses require approval.

audience.programmeDescription: Utrecht’s Global Sustainability Science bachelor combines natural science, social science and research methods. Students begin with a shared foundation and then deepen their study through one of five tracks.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The Utrecht example follows Water, Climate & Ecosystems. The closest UCR option focuses on water, climate and ecology. The other two options explore sustainability through governance and social change, or through business, energy and resource use.
